name: Business Case
one_liner: Why the project is worth doing — and worth continuing.
purpose: The Business Case captures the project's rationale, describes its alignment with the organisation's strategic objectives, justifies the investment in time and effort, and establishes budgetary needs. For larger strategic projects it also assesses impact and risks and carries a fuller cost-benefit analysis. It is a living document, re-examined at critical milestones to check that the expected benefits are still achievable and the project still relevant.
meta: IT governance artefact — mandatory for projects with an information system (p.25)
The PM² Business Case itself — PM²-Agile defines no agile variant
Unchanged PM² template; the agile guide refers you to the PM² Portal and Guide
PM² eight-column set (AGB·PSC·PO·BM·UR·SP·PM·PCT), not the agile six
Initiating; re-examined at critical project milestones
Project Charter · Architecture Overview · Operational Model · requirements (p.31)

fields.what: Why the project exists — the problem, need or opportunity, and the case for acting on it now.
fields.pollux: Eleven spreadsheets, four analysts, five days per quarter-end, and two open internal-audit findings on version control.

fields.what: How the project serves the organisation's strategy — the link decision-makers need before committing budget.
fields.pollux: Exposure transparency to the Board, Risk and national authorities, building directly on the delivered CASTOR platform.

fields.what: Justifies the investment in time and effort: what the organisation gets for the person-days and the money.
fields.pollux: 1,850 PD over 18 months to remove a five-day manual quarter-end and an audit exposure.

fields.what: Establishes the budget the project needs, by cost type and funding source, before approval is sought.
fields.pollux: €4.6 m total, in-house agile team plus two seconded contractor members from Levallois Systems.

fields.what: For larger strategic projects, an assessment of impact and risks alongside the cost-benefit analysis.
fields.pollux: National-authority access raises data-protection exposure; Brandeis (DPC) and Turing (LISO) flagged at Business Case stage.

fields.what: A more detailed cost-benefit analysis for larger strategic projects; the basis of 'is it worth doing'.
fields.pollux: Four analyst-weeks per quarter released, against €4.6 m over eighteen months of delivery.

fields.what: Measurable criteria the benefits will be judged against; they carry forward unchanged into the Project Charter.
fields.pollux: SC1–SC5, each with a baseline and a target, from pack assembly time to open audit findings.

fields.what: Do-nothing plus real options, each with a SWOT and qualitative assessment, and the chosen alternative named.
fields.pollux: Do nothing; extend CASTOR reporting screens; build a separate portal — the portal was chosen.

fields.what: High-level scope and the deliverables that will exist at the end — not yet decomposed into work items.
fields.pollux: One portal, reconciled exposure by member state, instrument and maturity, traceable to the lending platform.

fields.what: The high-level route from approval to benefits, later refined into the Charter's milestones and the Release Plan.
fields.pollux: Four quarterly releases across 2029, transition into service 31 Jan 2030.

fields.what: Names the Project Owner, the Solution Provider and the approving authority who signs the investment off.
fields.pollux: Nightingale (PO), da Vinci (SP), approving authority the Corporate Investment Board chaired by de' Medici.

fields.what: Re-examined at critical milestones: benefits still achievable, costs and schedule still within budget and timeline, project still relevant.
fields.pollux: Re-examined at the RfP and RfE gates and after Release 2's reconciliation panel changed scope.

fields.what: Its job is to give decision-makers what they need to decide whether the project is worth doing.
fields.pollux: De' Medici's question — funding something that cannot say what it will deliver — is answered here.

fields.what: The guide says to fully document the problem or need in the Business Case before gathering requirements (p.31).
fields.pollux: Nobody agrees what the exposure report should contain — stated as the problem, not deferred to requirements.

fields.what: With the Charter, it tells the Architecture Owner what problem is to be solved before any solution is drawn (pp.69, 71).
fields.pollux: Einstein starts every enabler discussion from the Business Case problem statement, not from a technology.

fields.what: Agile changes how Executing is run, not the governance layer: the Business Case stays mandatory and unchanged.
fields.who: PM explains it · PO owns it
fields.pollux: PM²-Agile does not replace PM²: Business Case, Charter, phases and gates all stay in POLLUX.

fields.what: AGB I · PSC C · PO A · BM R · UR C · SP S · PM S · PCT –. Eight PM² columns, not six.
fields.pollux: Hopper writes it; Nightingale signs for it; the PM only supports.

traps: PM is not Accountable here — the Project Owner is.
The BM writes the Business Case; the PM writes the Charter.
Agile does not delete or lighten the Business Case — it is mandatory.
Appendix B.2 prints BM = R, PM = S and shows no Accountable at all.
Business Case = why and whether; Project Charter = what, how and when.
